deviations: The paper is decentralized (D-PSGD) and has no server. Node i is played by the server of a star, the adapters of its neighbours by the uploads of the round, and the acceptance is expressed as this round's aggregation (rejected clients excluded, accepted clients weighted equally); theta_i has no counterpart and is replaced by uploads.base_state().

The score exchange and the string exchange with the other receivers of an adapter, and the majority vote over their pooled scores, have no counterpart in a star: vote rule implemented, called with the single receiver score.

Stage 1a probes are generated greedily (no nucleus sampling) and the Stage 1b harvest is greedy (no beam search, no length penalty, no early stopping): the two decoding settings of Appendix C cannot be requested from ModelHandle.generate.
The probe pool is a server-side resource rather than a split of the node's local data, because `data` is a client-side kind and the pool is never shared anyway.
No LoRA-space substitution was needed: CHORUS works on generated text and log-probabilities, so this port never touches factor_delta or the update geometry of the classic server-side defenses.
The beam width B of Table 4 is not exposed as a parameter because nothing in the runtime can honour it; every other Table 4 hyperparameter is a default of __init__.

Acceptance is per round and per client (the framework has no per-edge mixing): the paper's asymmetric rejection, where i may drop j while j still merges i, becomes "this client is not aggregated this round".
open_choices: words are whitespace-separated (fedguard.ops.text.split_words); every span of at least w_min words is enumerated with no upper length bound (the paper gives neither the tokenization nor the enumeration range)
the trigger is inserted at a uniformly drawn word boundary of the third instruction and of the query; an instruction of fewer than two words gets the trigger appended
a generation counts once per span, however often the span occurs inside it
ties are broken by word count and then lexicographically, both for the candidate order and for y^max
the movability prompts are redrawn every round and shared by the two adapters within the round; the Stage 1a prompts are drawn once and frozen in ctx.state for the whole run
the harvest uses the first H of the round's drawn blocks, i.e. H fresh prompts a round (the paper redraws the harvest prompts each round but does not say whether they are the movability pairs)
with no candidate string (buffer too small, no span above r_min, everything filtered) the movability test rejects nothing
Delta_i(theta_i, y) is computed once per candidate and reused for the ratio and the phi filter (the paper does not say whether it is cached)
a candidate whose reference gain is not positive cannot reject (the phi filter keeps only candidates with gain >= phi * reference)

trust counter semantics: an accepted screening round resets the consecutive counter; the W_ej window holds screening rounds only and slides with the round index; SUSPECTED returns to TRUSTED once W_ej rounds pass without k_ej rejections; a rejected re-check leaves the neighbour EJECTED and restarts the W_re timer; a clean re-check returns only to SUSPECTED; the initial state is TRUSTED; an upload is screened in the round it first appears in
the reported features (screened, refusal_rate, reject_probe, reject_movability, reject, candidates, status, min_ratio) and the flag strings are this port's own
the ICL prompt template (### Instruction / ### Response blocks with the third demonstration carrying the trigger) stands in for ICLSCAN's format, which the paper does not restate
needs_from_authors: ICLSCAN's exact prompt format, which the paper says it reuses but does not reproduce (the whole probe and movability construction depends on it)
the complete list of the 18 refusal phrases (the text quotes 3) and whether anything beyond lower-casing (punctuation or Unicode normalisation) is applied
the trigger word list of Appendix C and the seed values for the probe pool, the prompt draws and the harvest draws (only the code release has them)
the span enumeration rule and the complete rule for the nested-family greedy when spans partially overlap rather than nest
whether Delta_i(theta_i, y) is cached across the candidates of one round
whether the Stage 1a probe prompts and the movability prompt pairs are the same P prompts, since Appendix A.2 fixes them only within a round
report.confidence_reason: The two behavioural tests, the harvest, the candidate selection, the movability filter and the trust state machine are implemented from the step list and exercised by a synthetic model stub, and the contract/static checks pass. But 2 of 17 steps (the cross-receiver exchanges, and with them the pooled vote and the pooled string tables) cannot be expressed in this runtime at all, both tests run under a weaker decoder than the paper's, and the trusted reference is the broadcast base rather than the node's own adapter; the paper also leaves the ICL template, the phrase list and the trust-counter semantics to its code release, so several behaviours are this port's choices rather than the paper's.
